verdict.rationale: Alloy documents event-driven automation: event types can be mapped to Source Workflows that are automatically evaluated on submission. Its monitoring workflows apply policy logic and generate alerts or investigations when thresholds are met, with use cases such as interdicting transactions or rejecting unusual logins. However, the evidence for user-authored rule definition and the range of configurable actions is thin, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of how users define rule conditions, an explicit catalog of triggerable actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: any event can be submitted for additional monitoring by mapping the event type to a Source Workflow. When enabled, Alloy stores the data submitted on events and automatically routes all requests
Monitors transaction events in real time or at scheduled times to detect suspicious activity, apply policy logic, and generate alerts or investigations when thresholds are met.
Alloy supports dozens of use cases like interdicting on transactions, performing step-up after suspicious PII changes, or rejecting unusual login activity.
Alloy's Events API allows you to build a real-time integration for decisioning on suspicious ongoing behavior as soon as it happens.
